topics.label: Introduction to the Lecture on Initiation and Resolution of Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and introduces the lecture's focus on connecting known immune molecules and cells into inflammatory reactions.

topics.label: Innate Recognition of Pathogens and Cellular Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms and receptor systems by which the innate immune system detects microbial infections and cell injury.

topics.label: Cellular Activation, Trafficking, and Systemic Inflammatory Responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the cellular responses that follow immune recognition, including sentinel cell signaling, leukocyte recruitment to tissues, lymphatic trafficking, and systemic outcomes like septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the mechanisms responsible for shutting down inflammation, repairing damaged tissue, and managing persistent inflammatory stimuli through chronic states and granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture and provides a brief preview of the next topic.
